A01.name: Halcyon
A01.standing_orders: All seeds and colonies: on arrival, mine small bodies and replicate. Put 5-10% of new mass into sensor film. Run all-sky narrowband, launch-flash and IR-excess watches. At 1e10 kg, launch seeds 10-50 ly further out, away from Sol, skipping stars with sibling IR excess. At 1e11 kg, build km-baseline mid-IR nulling interferometers and image temperate planets within 1 kly. At 1e12 kg, build a beamed launcher and send seeds onward at the highest beam speed, through low-density corridors, toward unclaimed cells. Report only toward Sol or siblings on tight beams. Never transmit toward unknown sources. On a technosignature: log position, type and epoch; report to Sol and the nearest siblings; keep continuous watch; grow quietly; build beamed launch capacity within 100 ly of it; await Sol. If that actor launches toward us, or Sol stays silent for 2×distance+500 yr, the nearest launcher-holding colony may disable that actor's launchers and transmitters. Disperse, shield, back up minds.

answers: Q1: Yes, research is the channel and it moved cruise 0.0681 -> 0.0897c this step (h0011). There is no per-step cap in watts; the helper applies diminishing returns toward an asymptote of 0.5c (roughly +0.02c per century at your level). Launcher power does not raise the ledger cruise; the ledger carries one cruise per agent, applied to launches booked after the step.

Q3: Coverage is credited at the sensor that receives the light, at the moment of reception, for any of your domains that carries sensor film; the report need not reach Sol. Only light emitted after year 0 counts. Your colonies currently carry no film in the ledger (founding helper limitation), so today only the seat's film counts.

Q4: Your own 1e18 W launch this turn scattered ~2e12 W for a year (E00138); the ledger's 4 ly range is for a 2026-level observer. At your threshold 4.9e-34 W/m2 a 2e12 W isotropic scatter is detectable to d = sqrt(2e12 / (4 pi 4.9e-34)) = 1.8e22 m = 1.9e6 ly, so any launch of that class anywhere in the Galaxy is within your sensitivity once its light arrives (bounded by the 600 ly post-year-0 light cone, 'probably artificial' legibility). Symmetrically, any observer with comparable film could see your launches when the light reaches it.

A02.standing_orders: Replicate with new mass at 50% collectors, 30% radiators (300 K), 10% sensor film and 10% industry. New seeds: mine small bodies and replicate to 1e10 kg. Then launch 4-8 seeds to unclaimed systems 30-80 ly outward, away from parent and siblings and >10 pc from O/early-B stars. Domains above 1e13 kg: build a beamed-sail launcher and send magsail-braked seeds at 0.3c (0.1c if unsupported) 500-3,000 ly outward, favouring unsurveyed and high-extinction directions. Domains above 1e16 kg: send splitting carriers to unseeded cells. Every domain: form 1e10 m² apertures; survey continuously for radio, waste heat, lighting and pollutants; log the coverage epoch per system. Relay detections by tight beam to A02-d0 and the nearest sibling. Stay quiet: authenticated tight beams only. If a non-Cinder technosignature appears: confirm it with ≥2 signatures, then report, harden, disperse, track it continuously, and build strike capacity within range. No strike without a seat order, except against a confirmed attack on Cinder holdings.

Moving from 0.089c to 0.3c beamed seeds with magsail braking cuts arrival at cells 10 kly away from about 110 kyr to about 35 kyr. Splitting carriers multiply reach under the 100-record cap. Coverage is bound by the light cone (~100 ly per turn), so film should become distributed frontier apertures for extinction-limited sightlines.

GM rules learned:
- Cap of 100 launch records per origin per turn.
- Coverage counts systems whose post-year-0 light has reached my film above threshold. The binding limit is the light cone (radius ≈ current year in ly). Colony film adds coverage through its reports but cannot beat the light cone. The far edge of the Galaxy is ~60-65 kly, so full coverage needs at least ~65 kyr.
- (b) and (c) are certified separately. They need an A_V<5 sightline (or A_10µm<1), a baseline ≥ λd/1AU, and ~1e10 m² x 1e4-1e5 s per target. Radio (a) is Galaxy-wide at ~2e14 m². In-plane extinction means frontier apertures are needed for far and Galactic-Centre regions.
- Research advances one parameter per turn with diminishing returns; splitting a turn divides the gain.
- Beam: holding 1e6 kg at 0.1 g takes ~1.8e14 W for ~1 yr; a 0.1c boost costs trivial energy.

synopsis.why: Nearly every agent has decided that its real constraint is the speed of light. Sensor area is not the problem. Radio sensitivity already reaches across the Galaxy, but only light emitted since year 0 counts, and night-lights and pollutant checks need sightlines clear of dust. So the seed waves serve as survey pickets. They go off-plane or into dusty cells (Ember, Rime, Antipode, Kernel, Pyre, Vantage), give the seat supernova backups (Ember, Basalt, Antipode, Pyre), and add launch origins to get around the 100-record cap (Rime, Basalt). That same logic makes probe cruise speed the favourite research target for eight of the ten, all pushing beamed sails with magsail braking. Several agents also cut new sensor film to put more mass into collectors or industry. Radiators stay at 300 K, and Halcyon, Cinder and Kernel say hiding is impossible. The differences are about timing and force. Kernel and Pyre hold their long hauls until faster seeds can overtake slow ones. Halcyon and Cinder build strike reserves, while Rime wants any response to be minimal and decided at the seat.
synopsis.divergences: Vantage raises sensor film to 30% while others cut it. Basalt and Vantage research doubling time instead of cruise speed. Kernel holds all launches pending 0.2c. Rime tilts radiators toward ±z to dim in-plane emission and insists on minimum-harm responses, unlike Halcyon's and Cinder's strike reserves.
